name: NC-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Valerie Foushee running for reelection
Overwhelming fundraising and outside-spending advantage for Foushee
Prediction markets price Foushee near certain to win
model.rationale: The D+23 district, an incumbent seeking reelection, and a massive financial edge for Foushee all point the same direction, and markets price her at roughly 96% to win. The Republican challenger's negligible fundraising gives no basis to move off the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late surge in outside spending for the challenger or a polling surprise showing a single-digit race would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Carolina's 4th District is a solidly Democratic seat in the Research Triangle, with a partisan lean of about 23 points toward Democrats. Incumbent Valerie Foushee is running for reelection after easily securing her party's nomination. She has raised over $900,000 and benefits from roughly $2.4 million in outside support, while Republican Max Ganorkar has raised only about $12,000. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but has no visible campaign infrastructure.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing, both of which point strongly to Foushee. Prediction markets give her about a 96% chance of winning. A Republican upset would require an unprecedented collapse in this district; the realistic range of outcomes spans a comfortable Foushee win to a landslide.
